note: What a member answering for a bill says of it (src/director/press-comment-facts.ts, the on-record move set). Which parts of a member's position on a bill (legislature.ts MemberPosition, the reasons the floor cast their vote from) a member says out loud as their reason, the fact each becomes, and where a bill goes next by its status. Words only choose among records; nothing here is a number the world runs on.

saidReasons.spread: Which reasons are said: a member names their own views, the town, a section they won, their party or their last vote on the question; a lobby's push, a bribe, ambition and temperament move votes but are not what a member tells a reporter. Order breaks a tie.
saidReasons.checkedAgainst: Fenno, Home Style (1978), on how members explain votes to constituents: policy belief, constituency wishes and party are the explanations offered; the press-comment arcs' own reasons on main before Nov 12.

reasonFacts.spread: Names only; one fact per said reason.
reasonFacts.checkedAgainst: The pieces of the on-record set that require each fact.

laterByForm.spread: Words only: how a measure is said after its name, by its form (BillRow.form.kind).
laterByForm.checkedAgainst: data/english/bill-names.json forms; the coordinator's note of Nov 12 ("after that 'it', 'the ordinance'").

nextByStatus.spread: Names only; one fact per stage a bill can be in after a call.
